section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports a single study (Study X) of undergraduate women (N = 143) who completed self-report measures of exercise behavior, body orientation, body appreciation, and body-related talk. Results indicate that conversations about exercise versus weight loss/dieting differentially predict body appreciation, with exercise conversations promoting an object orientation that in turn predicted higher body appreciation, whereas weight-loss conversations related to body appreciation via negative attitudes about the body.
